negative_reviews.author: Noth
negative_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, Ramen Ichiramen no longer offers a regular, non-halal Steak Tataki Ramen. Previously, customers could choose between halal and non-halal beef, but now the website states that all beef used in their ramen is halal, leaving customers with no alternative.

I believe this is unfair to customers who, for personal or religious reasons, do not wish to consume halal meat. As a Christian, I do not believe I should be expected to accept a religiously prepared product when I previously had the option to choose otherwise.

I fully respect the right of Muslim customers to choose halal food. However, I believe the same consideration should be given to customers who prefer non-halal meat. Previously, both options were available, but now only halal beef is offered, meaning that customers who do not want halal meat have lost their choice.

In my opinion, a restaurant should respect the different dietary preferences and beliefs of all its customers rather than remove an option that was previously available.

Unfortunately, this change has left me disappointed. I would like to see Ramen Ichiramen reintroduce the non-halal beef option for its Steak Tataki Ramen.

One star due to the loss of choice and the lack of consideration for customers who do not wish to eat halal meat.

issues: Covers were 1,346, down 156 week on week and up 5 year on year.
Spend per head fell to £15.90, down £1.67 week on week and £9.42 year on year, plummeting because of the discounts; covers may not be adjusted when bills are split, which will be monitored.
Customers coming in mainly for £5 ramens are not buying extras and only take tap water, with a huge swell in students.
Sales were £26,706.02 against the £30,000 target, down £5,695.83 (17.57%) week on week and £11,478.24 (30.06%) year on year.
Deliveroo is spiking at weekends with the 50% off promo, which runs for a couple more weeks.

Deliveroo rejected orders rose because orders came in while the team was still cleaning up after the pump flooded the kitchen and BOH area, and late prep was higher than wanted, mainly over the weekend with the home match.
The site's Deliveroo account shows no figures or refunds, and Matt has messaged Junna for new login details since the company change.
Labour: absolute minimal hours in play, £561.17 less spent than the previous week and 48.4 hours dropped.
With the discounts needing extra product, the Deliveroo discount needing extra packaging and free frozen ramen to order, Erin did very well to keep food spend low; food variance -3% and drinks -2%.
Google reviews: 22 five star, 3 four star and 1 one star.
Compliance: pest control, fire, electrical, gas and ventilation completed (ventilation visit on 1 October).
Maintenance: air con and front door ultra high priority (Ross and Cheska), accessible lift medium (logged), female toilet high (logged, Kris) and walk in freezer ultra high (logged, Kris).
Neither Kris nor his support could fix the front door, which has to stay permanently open on a site without real heating, so it is getting very cold.
Water is dripping badly into the freezer; photos have been sent to Oisin and Ross.

Staffing: Olsi is back this week, Ben, Drew and Kin have time off coming up, Abigail has been hired for FOH and starts next week, and BOH trials are later this week to fill one kitchen assistant role.
Hiring and training the new team and setting up the team for Christmas are the stated areas for improvement.
Upcoming: 50% off Deliveroo Friday to Sunday, frozen ramen next week, the new broth and product later this month and Teddy's book launch.
The Newcastle Bottomless Brunch will end after the next couple of weeks (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: Rebecca reported a Scotland sales uptick from the school holidays (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: the 50% off and free ramen app vouchers end at the end of the month, while £5 ramen vouchers stay downloadable for new accounts in the short term and will be honoured (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: XOXO drinks move to the main menu and will no longer be tracked separately (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: 3,000 book copies have arrived at the office for distribution to sites by 12 November (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: digital Brix refractometers read well below manual tests (Maki 8 digital 5 against manual 6.5 to 7), so Michael mandated daily cleaning and calibration (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: incoming POS orders jumping straight to finished, delivered or preparing have been reported to Kobas and Deliverect, and Inka is changing the POS settings (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: a scalable beef solution is rolling out by the end of the month after product that did not match the approved specs was received (Admin Meeting 19/10).

Region: the factory sous vide chicken looked red because the recipe sheet used 3% soy instead of 1%; ingredients, taste, texture and slice size are approved, and restaurants sign off only once they see the finished, sliced and packed product (factory call 20/10).
Total discounts and staff food were over £6,000, and sales missed target for the first time in over a month (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Upcoming rotas are complete thanks to Emma (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).

With the automatic front door broken and stuck open, the downstairs seating will be unusable by the end of October, and the original installers will no longer service the door because it is too old (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
The air conditioning unit above Sakura is hard to access; Ka Ho asked for Ross's approval to send someone down from Scotland for a full assessment (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Frozen ramen stock is ready to use (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: GMs must attend the GM and head chef meeting in person or send a designated representative (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: all sites will move to recorded meetings (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).

Region: Michael plans to roll out the control centre dashboard to every site in the region over the next few days, with Rory guiding the other GMs; Ka Ho will confirm the rollout and logins with Michael on Wednesday (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Labour rose to 25.38% from 22.73%, the highest of the nine Scotland and Newcastle sites, and food cost was 25.93%, down from 27.22% (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Erin said sales dropped slightly because of a problem with the cooker (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Discounts cost about £6,000, and large tables booked just for £5 ramen left average spend the second lowest in the group (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
The basement walk in freezer is leaking from the pipe above; the engineer could not fix it, so a bucket is catching the water until Kris inspects, expected on Friday (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).

True World Fish sent only tuna and sea bream on 16/10, with tamago, masago, soft shell crab and sushi ebi missing; the £64.84 issue is closed after the driver returned (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).

A 1 star review on 17/10 objected that the non halal tataki ramen is no longer offered; the same text was posted at Metrocentre and is thought to be one reviewer, and Matt said only the broth changed, not the meat (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Rider wait time is red (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: Michael made rider wait time the priority delivery metric this week, followed by ratings; sites need a 4.7 Deliveroo rating to compete and open times above 99.5% (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: GMs and head chefs must run a daily morning brief for FOH and BOH using the app's daily tab to review sales, delivery ratings and setups (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: failed delivery orders come from items marked out of stock on Kobas but not on Deliverect, so managers must update both, snooze unavailable extras by PLU and check Deliverect failed order statuses daily (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: stock edit permissions will be suspended for one week to see true variances, after wastage and comps were used to bring variances under 5% and distort Kobas ordering baselines (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: from next week automated Gemini meeting recordings and dashboard sign offs replace manual meeting notes and KPI sheets, with tasks synced to Asana and the legacy spreadsheets kept as a backup for now (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: third party discounted bookings are no longer allowed on Saturdays and are capped at a share of capacity on other days (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: Hungry Panda still has untranslated menu text, wrong integrations and overridden PLUs; Sophie is to fix the setup, and Michael suggested turning it off if it hurts Deliveroo and Slerp without enough revenue (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: ramen bowls are now ordered only from Harro, not Lynas (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).

Region: Teddy confirmed that during the app promotions sites may buy extra stock and ask Matt or Penny for extra kitchen hours, as the discounts are marketing for another 25,000 app sign ups (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: frozen ramen stock is limited and sites ran short last week, so Penny asked sites to check availability; no extra labour budget has been given for it (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: Lynas did not reply to any delivery issue report last week; 17 supplier issues across Scotland and Newcastle left £385.55 of credit due (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
